# Introduction

Cell proportions are often measured more than once in the same donor, across tumour cores or serial biopsies. The resulting observations are correlated. Averaging the cores removes ROI-level variation, while testing each phenotype separately ignores that the proportions must sum to one.

We use [sccomp](https://github.com/MangiolaLaboratory/sccomp), a Bayesian compositional model that accepts mixed-effects designs. We fitted sccomp to a long tibble of cell counts, with one row per sample and cell type, tested the fitted model with contrasts, and predicted cell-type proportions.


# Source study and study design

We apply [sccomp](https://github.com/MangiolaLaboratory/sccomp) to the NeoTRIP trial. [Wang *et al.* (2023)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06498-3) used imaging mass cytometry (IMC) to map how multicellular spatial organization in triple-negative breast cancer relates to neoadjuvant immunotherapy response. In the phase III NeoTRIP trial (NCT02620280), early high-risk TNBC patients were randomised 1:1 to carboplatin + nab-paclitaxel (C) or the same regimen plus atezolizumab (C&I) for eight 3-week neoadjuvant cycles before surgery. Research FFPE biopsies:

- Baseline (*n* = 243)
- On-treatment (first day of cycle 2; *n* = 207)
- Post-treatment (surgical excision; *n* = 210)
- Profiled with a 43-marker IMC panel at subcellular resolution
- Deep-learning segmentation and semi-supervised clustering defined 17 epithelial and 20 TME cell phenotypes
- Multiple regions of interest (ROIs) were imaged per biopsy

Each patient contributes several samples. The biopsies are nested in the patient, and the regions of interest are nested in the biopsy. Patient NT193, in the chemotherapy arm with residual disease, was imaged at all three timepoints: 10 ROIs at baseline, 10 on-treatment, and 3 at surgery. In the model, each ROI is one compositional sample and the patient is the repeated-measures group.

```{r fig-nesting}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "One patient, three timepoints, several ROIs"
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.4
#| fig-alt: "Tree for patient NT193. The patient sits at the top and three biopsy timepoints branch underneath. Each timepoint ends in the imaged regions of interest, drawn as spatial tiles: magenta M2 macrophages, yellow PD-L1-positive antigen-presenting cells, and green other immune cells. There are 10 tiles at baseline, 10 on-treatment, and 3 post-treatment."

mk_spatial_tile <- function(dat, square = TRUE, pt = c(other = 0.10, pdl1 = 0.16, m2 = 0.16)) {
  if (nrow(dat) == 0) {
    dat <- tibble::tibble(
      Location_Center_X = numeric(),
      Location_Center_Y = numeric(),
      draw = character()
    )
  }
  tile <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = Location_Center_X, y = Location_Center_Y)) +
    geom_point(data = filter(dat, draw == "other"), colour = "#39FF14", size = pt[["other"]]) +
    geom_point(data = filter(dat, draw == "pdl1"), colour = "#FFFF00", size = pt[["pdl1"]]) +
    geom_point(data = filter(dat, draw == "m2"), colour = "#FF00FF", size = pt[["m2"]]) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = NULL, guide = "none", expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_reverse(labels = NULL, guide = "none", expand = c(0, 0)) +
    theme_void(base_size = 8) +
    theme(
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "black", colour = NA),
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.margin = margin(
        if (square) 1 else 0, if (square) 1 else 0,
        if (square) 1 else 0, if (square) 1 else 0,
        unit = "pt"
      )
    )
  if (square) tile <- tile + theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
  tile
}

  summarise(x = mean(x), .by = BiopsyPhase) |>

patient <- tibble::tibble(

edges <- bind_rows(

for (i in seq_len(nrow(roi))) {
```

Wang *et al.* linked cell densities, spatial interactions, and proliferative fractions to pathological complete response (pCR), and showed that immunotherapy remodels tissue composition over time, with response-specific dynamics of immune infiltration (notably in their Fig. 5 compositional trajectory analysis).

| Quantity | Value |
|----------|------:|
| Per-protocol patients | 257 |
| ROI-level immune samples | 1,740 |
| Immune cell phenotypes | 15 |
| Median ROIs per patient | 7 |

# sccomp mixed-effects compositional modelling

Wang *et al.* summarised longitudinal composition as mean phenotype proportions per patient and compared arms, timepoints, and response groups with Wilcoxon tests, *Z*-scored trend plots (their Fig. 5), and per-phenotype weighted binomial GLMs on tumour-level proportions. Those tests treat each phenotype in isolation and average ROIs to the patient before inference, setting aside compositional closure (proportions sum to one) and the nesting of biopsies and ROIs within patients.

With [sccomp](https://github.com/MangiolaLaboratory/sccomp), we model the ROI-level cell counts directly on a latent log-ratio scale with mixed effects on the mean and variability. Each ROI is one compositional sample (`sample = "ROI_id"` in `sccomp_estimate()`), several ROIs share a biopsy timepoint (`BiopsyPhase`), and a patient random intercept `(1 | PatientID)` accounts for baseline differences across individuals and shrinkage across the cohort:

$$\text{composition} \sim \text{Arm} \times \text{BiopsyPhase} \times \text{pCR} + (1 \mid \text{PatientID})$$


# sccomp analysis

To retain the information from individual ROIs while accounting for repeated samples from the same patient, we analysed the immune TME compartment with each ROI as a sample and included a patient random intercept. The code can be run from top to bottom from the parsed input.

## From long-format tidy input

The input `long` is a tibble with one row per ROI × immune phenotype: `ROI_id`, a count, the design columns (`Arm`, `BiopsyPhase`, `pCR`), and the grouping `PatientID`. Several ROIs share one `BiopsyPhase`. Preview:

```{r repro-long-preview}
#| code-fold: show
#| code-summary: "Load long-format input"
#| cache: true
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

long <- read_csv(file.path(results_dir, "sccomp_long_tme_immune_roi.csv"),
                 show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  rename(ROI_id = sample) |>
  mutate(
    count = as.integer(count),
    BiopsyPhase = factor(BiopsyPhase, c("Baseline", "On-treatment", "Post-treatment")),
    Arm = factor(Arm, c("C", "C&I")),
    pCR = factor(pCR, c("RD", "pCR"))
  )

long |>
  select(ROI_id, cell_group, count, PatientID, BiopsyPhase, Arm, pCR) |>
  gt::gt_preview() |>
  gt::tab_caption("Long-format sccomp input (1,740 ROIs x 15 immune phenotypes)")
```

## Fit the model

To estimate response-associated changes across treatment arms and biopsy timepoints, we fitted the mixed-effects compositional model specified above.

```{r repro-sccomp-fit-code}
#| ref.label: repro-sccomp-fit
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
```

```{r repro-sccomp-fit}
#| code-fold: show
#| code-summary: "Fit and test the model"
#| cache: true
#| cache.lazy: false
#| dependson: "repro-long-preview"
#| cache.extra: !expr as.character(packageVersion("sccomp"))
library(sccomp)

fit <- sccomp_estimate(
  long,
  formula_composition = ~ Arm * BiopsyPhase * pCR + (1 | PatientID),
  formula_variability = ~ 1,
  sample = "ROI_id",
  cell_group = "cell_group",
  abundance = "count",
  inference_method = "hmc",
  cores = parallel::detectCores(),
  verbose = FALSE
) |>
  sccomp_test()
```

```{r repro-fit-print-sccomp}
#| echo: false
fit
```

We used `sccomp_proportional_fold_change()` to calculate how the fitted proportions changed between two conditions. We treated this as a descriptive result and used `sccomp_test()` for significance. Here, we compare residual disease with pathological complete response after chemoimmunotherapy at surgery:

```{r repro-proportional-fold-change}
#| code-fold: show
#| code-summary: "Proportional fold change"
#| cache: true
#| dependson: "repro-sccomp-fit"
fit |>
  sccomp_proportional_fold_change(
    formula_composition = ~ Arm * BiopsyPhase * pCR,
    from = "C&I:Post-treatment:RD",  # chemoimmunotherapy, surgery, residual disease
    to = "C&I:Post-treatment:pCR"    # same arm and visit, pathological complete response
  ) |>
  gt::gt_preview() |>
  gt::tab_caption(
    "Proportional fold change: C&I post-treatment, pCR versus residual disease"
  )
```

## Model checks

**Convergence.** To check the HMC sampling, we inspected $\hat{R}$ and effective sample sizes. All 4,035 composition parameters have median $\hat{R}$ = 1.001 (maximum 1.014). Bulk effective sample size has median 4,837 (minimum 495). Tail effective sample size has median 2,850 (minimum 923).

Variability is an intercept for each phenotype. Those 15 coefficients have maximum $\hat{R}$ = 1.003, minimum bulk ESS 3,404, and minimum tail ESS 2,451. The composition parameters with the smallest bulk ESS:

```{r repro-convergence}
#| code-fold: show
#| code-summary: "Smallest bulk effective sample sizes"
fit |>
  filter(is.finite(c_ess_bulk)) |>
  slice_min(c_ess_bulk, n = 6, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  gt::gt_preview() |>
  gt::tab_caption(
    "Composition parameters with the smallest bulk effective sample size"
  )
```

**Posterior predictive check.** To check whether the fitted model reproduces the observed distributions, we compared adjusted proportions with posterior predictive replicates. We set `remove_unwanted_effects = TRUE` to retain variation associated with biopsy timepoint. The black boxes are adjusted proportions, the blue boxes are posterior predictive replicates, and fill marks a timepoint contrast with FDR below 0.05.

```{r repro-ppc}
#| code-fold: false
#| code-summary: "Posterior predictive check"
#| results: hide
#| cache: true
#| dependson: "repro-sccomp-fit"
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-width: 10
#| dpi: 100
#| fig-retina: 1
#| fig-alt: "Boxplots of immune-cell proportions by biopsy timepoint, faceted by cell type, after removing variation other than biopsy timepoint. Black boxes are adjusted proportions and blue boxes are posterior predictive replicates. Filled boxes mark a timepoint contrast with FDR below 0.05."
fit |> 
  sccomp_boxplot(
  factor = "BiopsyPhase",
  significance_statistic = "FDR",
  remove_unwanted_effects = TRUE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Posterior predictive check",
    subtitle = "Black: adjusted proportions. Blue: replicates from the fitted model.",
    x = "Biopsy timepoint"
  ) +
  guides(colour = "none", shape = "none") 
```

## Hypothesis testing

We pass contrasts to `sccomp_test()` as strings. 

With `marginal_CI_post`, we compared responders with patients with residual disease at the post-treatment visit. This comparison retains any difference already present at baseline.

With `did_CI_post`, we compared their changes from baseline, thereby accounting for the difference already present at baseline. We use this contrast because a visit-only comparison retains that difference. Post-treatment M2 proportions are similar in the two response groups, so the post-treatment snapshot alone does not describe the change.

```{r repro-contrasts}
#| code-fold: show
#| code-summary: "Test two contrasts"
#| cache: true
#| dependson: "repro-sccomp-fit"
contrasts <- c(
  marginal_CI_post = paste(
    "`pCRpCR`",                                  # pCR versus RD in chemotherapy at baseline
    "`ArmC&I:pCRpCR`",                           # additional pCR versus RD gap in the C&I arm
    "`BiopsyPhasePost-treatment:pCRpCR`",        # additional pCR versus RD gap at post-treatment
    "`ArmC&I:BiopsyPhasePost-treatment:pCRpCR`", # additional pCR versus RD gap for C&I at post-treatment
    sep = " + "
  ),
  did_CI_post = paste(
    "`BiopsyPhasePost-treatment:pCRpCR`",        # change from baseline in the pCR contrast
    "`ArmC&I:BiopsyPhasePost-treatment:pCRpCR`", # further change from baseline in the C&I arm
    sep = " + "
  )
)

res <- sccomp_test(fit, contrasts = contrasts)
```

We stored both contrasts in `res`, with one row per phenotype. Below, we list the full set of difference-in-differences, strongest first:

```{r repro-did-preview}
#| code-fold: show
#| code-summary: "Preview difference-in-differences contrasts"
hmc_did |>
  filter(contrast_family == "did") |>
  arrange(c_FDR) |>
  gt::gt_preview() |>
  gt::tab_caption("Change from baseline (strongest by FDR)")
```

# Results

## Predicted immune compositional trajectories

To compare the trajectories from a common starting point, we aligned both response groups to the mean of their baseline predictions for each treatment arm and cell type. We plot the predicted proportions and 95% credible intervals for all 15 immune TME phenotypes. Columns separate the treatment arms, colours separate the response groups, and asterisks mark difference-in-differences with FDR \< 0.05.

```{r repro-baseline-aligned}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Align groups to a common baseline"
#| cache: true
#| dependson:
#|   - repro-sccomp-fit
#|   - repro-predictions-population
# Plot shift. Within each arm and cell type, move pCR and RD to the mean of
# their baseline predictions, on the posterior draws.
draws <- sccomp_predict(
  fit, new_data = pop, number_of_draws = 500, summary_instead_of_draws = FALSE
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(across(c(Arm, BiopsyPhase, pCR), as.character))

# Shift pCR and RD to their average baseline within each Arm x cell_group, per draw
shifts <- draws |>
  filter(BiopsyPhase == "Baseline") |>
  select(Arm, cell_group, .draw, pCR, proportion) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = pCR, values_from = proportion) |>
  mutate(shift_pCR = (pCR + RD) / 2 - pCR,
         shift_RD  = (pCR + RD) / 2 - RD) |>
  select(Arm, cell_group, .draw, shift_pCR, shift_RD)

aligned_summary <- draws |>
  left_join(shifts, by = c("Arm", "cell_group", ".draw")) |>
  mutate(aligned_prop = proportion + if_else(pCR == "pCR", shift_pCR, shift_RD)) |>
  summarise(
    aligned_mean  = mean(aligned_prop),
    aligned_lower = quantile(aligned_prop, 0.025),
    aligned_upper = quantile(aligned_prop, 0.975),
    .by = c(Arm, BiopsyPhase, pCR, cell_group)
  )
```

```{r fig-main-trajectories}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Baseline-aligned immune trajectories"
#| fig-height: 18
#| fig-width: 10
#| dpi: 100
#| fig-retina: 1
#| fig-alt: "Line plots of baseline-aligned immune proportions across biopsy timepoints, faceted by cell type and treatment arm, with pathological complete response and residual disease in separate colours and asterisks where the difference-in-differences FDR is below 0.05."

cell_order <- c(
  "CD8^+T", "CD8^+GZMB^+T", "CD8^+TCF1^+T", "CD8^+PD1^+T_{Ex}",
  "CD4^+TCF1^+T", "CD4^+PD1^+T", "Treg", "CD20^+B", "CD79a^+Plasma",
  "CD56^+NK", "M2 Mac", "DCs", "Neutrophils", "PD-L1^+APCs", "PD-L1^+IDO^+APCs"
)
cols_response <- c(RD = "#377EB8", pCR = "#E41A1C")

pred_main <- aligned_summary |>
  mutate(
    BiopsyPhase = factor(BiopsyPhase, phase_levels),
    Arm = factor(Arm, arm_levels),
    pCR = factor(pCR, c("RD", "pCR")),
    cell_group = factor(cell_group, levels = cell_order),
    # A few intervals sit just below zero after the baseline shift.
    aligned_mean = pmax(aligned_mean, 0),
    aligned_lower = pmax(aligned_lower, 0)
  )

# Asterisk just above the ribbon where the DiD FDR is below 0.05.
did_sig_fig1 <- hmc_did |>
  filter(contrast_family == "did", is.finite(c_FDR), c_FDR < 0.05) |>
  distinct(cell_group, Arm, BiopsyPhase) |>
  mutate(cell_group = factor(cell_group, levels = cell_order)) |>
  inner_join(
    pred_main |>
      summarise(ymax = max(aligned_upper), .by = c(cell_group, Arm, BiopsyPhase)),
    by = c("cell_group", "Arm", "BiopsyPhase")
  )

ggplot(pred_main, aes(x = BiopsyPhase, y = aligned_mean, colour = pCR, group = pCR)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = aligned_lower, ymax = aligned_upper, fill = pCR),
    alpha = 0.10, colour = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.75) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  geom_text(
    data = did_sig_fig1,
    aes(x = BiopsyPhase, y = ymax, label = "*"),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4.5, colour = "black", fontface = "bold", vjust = -0.2
  ) +
  facet_grid(cell_group ~ Arm, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.01)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols_response, name = "Response") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols_response, name = "Response") +
  labs(
    title = "Baseline-aligned immune compositional trajectories",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Baseline-aligned predicted proportion"
  ) +
  theme_pub() +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(size = 7))
```


## Change from baseline

For each cell type and treatment arm, we test whether responders and patients with residual disease changed by different amounts from baseline. We plotted these contrasts for the on-treatment and post-treatment visits in **Figure 2**; borders mark FDR \< 0.05.

```{r fig-did-heatmap}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Difference-in-differences heatmap"
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-alt: "Heatmap of difference-in-differences effects, on the centered log-ratio scale, for each immune phenotype, treatment arm, and post-baseline visit. Black borders mark FDR below 0.05."

did_hm <- hmc_did |>
  filter(contrast_family == "did") |>
  mutate(
    cell_group = factor(cell_group, levels = rev(cell_order)),
    BiopsyPhase = factor(BiopsyPhase, levels = c("On-treatment", "Post-treatment")),
    Arm = factor(Arm, arm_levels)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(cell_group)) |>
  mutate(
    sig = is.finite(c_FDR) & c_FDR < 0.05,
    facet_lab = factor(
      paste(Arm, BiopsyPhase, sep = " · "),
      levels = c(
        "C · On-treatment", "C · Post-treatment",
        "C&I · On-treatment", "C&I · Post-treatment"
      )
    )
  )

lim <- max(abs(did_hm$c_effect), na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(did_hm, aes(x = facet_lab, y = cell_group, fill = c_effect)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_tile(
    data = filter(did_hm, sig),
    colour = "black", linewidth = 0.7, fill = NA
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = if_else(sig, sprintf("%.2f", c_effect), "")),
    size = 2.6
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = cols_response[["RD"]], mid = "white", high = cols_response[["pCR"]],
    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-lim, lim), name = "Effect on\ncentered log-ratio scale"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Response-associated change from baseline (difference-in-differences)",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_pub() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```

**Finding:** Under the difference-in-differences contrast, 14 immune phenotypes change from baseline at post-treatment, and 9 at the on-treatment visit.

**Finding:** In the chemoimmunotherapy arm at post-treatment, M2 macrophages increase more from baseline in patients who reach pathological complete response (FDR 0.007), while PD-L1-positive antigen-presenting cells decrease (FDR < 0.0002).

**Finding:** The M2 macrophage change is not detected at the on-treatment visit (FDR 0.21).

## M2 macrophage changes by response

To show how the visit-specific comparison differs from the change-from-baseline analysis, we compared both M2 macrophage contrasts. Grey points compare pCR with residual disease at a single visit, whereas red points compare their changes from baseline. Points above the dotted line have FDR \< 0.05.

```{r fig-volcano}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "M2 macrophage changes by response"
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of M2 macrophage response contrasts, with the centered log-ratio effect on the x-axis and minus log10 FDR on the y-axis, comparing pCR versus residual disease at each visit with the change from baseline."

m2_volcano <- bind_rows(
  hmc_marginal_pcr |>
    filter(cell_group == "M2 Mac") |>
    mutate(Arm, BiopsyPhase, c_effect, c_FDR, family = "Marginal pCR vs RD"),
  hmc_did |>
    filter(contrast_family == "did", cell_group == "M2 Mac") |>
    mutate(Arm, BiopsyPhase, c_effect, c_FDR, family = "DiD (change from T0)")
) |>
  mutate(label = paste(Arm, BiopsyPhase, sep = " · "))

ggplot(m2_volcano, aes(x = c_effect, y = -log10(pmax(c_FDR, 1e-12)))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = 2, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = family, shape = BiopsyPhase), size = 2.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.3, vjust = -0.9, colour = "grey25") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    "Marginal pCR vs RD" = "#999999",
    "DiD (change from T0)" = "#d73027"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "M2 Mac: visit contrast and change from baseline",
    x = "Effect on centered log-ratio scale",
    y = expression(-log[10](FDR)),
    colour = NULL, shape = NULL
  ) +
  theme_pub()
```

## Between-patient heterogeneity in M2 Mac

To show how patients vary around the population trajectory, we estimated the population pattern using fixed effects and allowed each patient's predictions to shift up or down using a random intercept. We did not estimate separate patient-specific slopes. We plot the resulting per-patient M2 macrophage predictions below.

```{r fig-patient-heterogeneity}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Between-patient M2 trajectories"
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-alt: "Line plots of predicted M2 macrophage proportion for each patient across biopsy timepoints, faceted by treatment arm and pathological response."

pred_pat <- hmc_pred_patient |>
  filter(cell_group == "M2 Mac") |>
  mutate(cell_group = factor(cell_group))

pcr_cols <- c("RD" = "#4575b4", "pCR" = "#d73027")

ggplot(pred_pat, aes(x = BiopsyPhase, y = proportion_mean, group = PatientID, colour = pCR)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(cell_group ~ Arm + pCR, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pcr_cols, name = "Response") +
  labs(
    title = "Between-patient variation in predicted M2 Mac proportion",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Predicted proportion"
  ) +
  theme_pub() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

## The change on the tissue

As examples of the estimated effects, we selected four patients with paired biopsies. These examples show the direction of the contrast; the cohort estimates above give its magnitude.

Baseline regions are on the left and regions from the surgical specimen are on the right. Because they are different pieces of tissue, we compare cell-type proportions across biopsies. In these selected examples, the responders gain M2 macrophages and lose PD-L1-positive antigen-presenting cells, whereas the residual-disease patients change little. Magenta marks M2 macrophages, yellow marks PD-L1-positive antigen-presenting cells, and green marks other immune cells.

```{r fig-m2-spatial}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Baseline and post-treatment maps for four patients"
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8.6
#| dpi: 130
#| fig-retina: 1
#| fig-alt: "Four chemoimmunotherapy patients, each shown at baseline and at post-treatment. Two responders gain magenta M2 macrophages and lose yellow PD-L1-positive antigen-presenting cells. Two patients with residual disease, matched to a similar baseline M2 level, look about the same at both visits. Green marks other immune cells."

cells <- read_fst(file.path(post_dir, "did-example-cells.fst")) |> as_tibble()

examples <- tibble::tribble(
  ~PatientID, ~response, ~BiopsyPhase,       ~ImageID,    ~prop,
  "NT218",    "pCR",     "Baseline",         "NTImg1578", "M2 4.0%\nPD-L1+ APCs 12.3%",
  "NT218",    "pCR",     "Baseline",         "NTImg1579", "M2 4.0%\nPD-L1+ APCs 12.3%",
  "NT218",    "pCR",     "Baseline",         "NTImg1580", "M2 4.0%\nPD-L1+ APCs 12.3%",
  "NT218",    "pCR",     "Post-treatment",   "NTImg0491", "M2 42.4%\nPD-L1+ APCs 0.7%",
  "NT218",    "pCR",     "Post-treatment",   "NTImg0493", "M2 42.4%\nPD-L1+ APCs 0.7%",
  "NT215",    "pCR",     "Baseline",         "NTImg1181", "M2 11.1%\nPD-L1+ APCs 10.2%",
  "NT215",    "pCR",     "Baseline",         "NTImg1182", "M2 11.1%\nPD-L1+ APCs 10.2%",
  "NT215",    "pCR",     "Baseline",         "NTImg1183", "M2 11.1%\nPD-L1+ APCs 10.2%",
  "NT215",    "pCR",     "Post-treatment",   "NTImg0366", "M2 45.8%\nPD-L1+ APCs 0.4%",
  "NT215",    "pCR",     "Post-treatment",   "NTImg0372", "M2 45.8%\nPD-L1+ APCs 0.4%",
  "NT215",    "pCR",     "Post-treatment",   "NTImg0378", "M2 45.8%\nPD-L1+ APCs 0.4%",
  "NT174",    "RD",      "Baseline",         "NTImg1824", "M2 2.0%\nPD-L1+ APCs 2.1%",
  "NT174",    "RD",      "Baseline",         "NTImg1825", "M2 2.0%\nPD-L1+ APCs 2.1%",
  "NT174",    "RD",      "Baseline",         "NTImg1826", "M2 2.0%\nPD-L1+ APCs 2.1%",
  "NT174",    "RD",      "Post-treatment",   "NTImg0540", "M2 1.6%\nPD-L1+ APCs 0.8%",
  "NT174",    "RD",      "Post-treatment",   "NTImg0542", "M2 1.6%\nPD-L1+ APCs 0.8%",
  "NT028",    "RD",      "Baseline",         "NTImg1317", "M2 12.3%\nPD-L1+ APCs 1.8%",
  "NT028",    "RD",      "Baseline",         "NTImg1318", "M2 12.3%\nPD-L1+ APCs 1.8%",
  "NT028",    "RD",      "Baseline",         "NTImg1319", "M2 12.3%\nPD-L1+ APCs 1.8%",
  "NT028",    "RD",      "Post-treatment",   "NTImg0385", "M2 12.6%\nPD-L1+ APCs 1.9%",
  "NT028",    "RD",      "Post-treatment",   "NTImg0387", "M2 12.6%\nPD-L1+ APCs 1.9%"
)

tile_pt <- c(other = 0.22, pdl1 = 0.40, m2 = 0.40)

mk_note <- function(text, size = 2.7, face = "plain") {
  ggplot() +
    annotate(
      "text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = text,
      fontface = face, size = size, lineheight = 0.95
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    theme_void()
}

mk_phase <- function(pid, phase) {
  ids <- examples |>
    filter(PatientID == pid, BiopsyPhase == phase) |>
    pull(ImageID)
  ids <- c(ids, rep(NA_character_, 3L - length(ids)))
  tiles <- lapply(ids, function(id) {
    if (is.na(id)) return(patchwork::plot_spacer())
    mk_spatial_tile(filter(cells, ImageID == id), pt = tile_pt)
  })
  prop <- examples$prop[examples$PatientID == pid & examples$BiopsyPhase == phase][1]
  patchwork::wrap_plots(
    mk_note(prop, size = 2.5),
    patchwork::wrap_plots(tiles, nrow = 1),
    ncol = 1,
    heights = c(0.22, 1)
  )
}

mk_patient <- function(pid) {
  response <- examples$response[examples$PatientID == pid][1]
  patchwork::wrap_plots(
    mk_note(paste0(pid, "\n", response), size = 3.1, face = "bold"),
    mk_phase(pid, "Baseline"),
    mk_phase(pid, "Post-treatment"),
    nrow = 1,
    widths = c(0.55, 3, 3)
  )
}

header <- patchwork::wrap_plots(
  patchwork::plot_spacer(),
  mk_note("Baseline", size = 3.4, face = "bold"),
  mk_note("Post-treatment", size = 3.4, face = "bold"),
  nrow = 1,
  widths = c(0.55, 3, 3)
)

patchwork::wrap_plots(
  header,
  mk_patient("NT218"),
  mk_patient("NT215"),
  mk_patient("NT174"),
  mk_patient("NT028"),
  ncol = 1,
  heights = c(0.28, 1, 1, 1, 1)
) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Change from baseline in four chemoimmunotherapy patients",
    subtitle = "Magenta: M2 macrophages.  Yellow: PD-L1-positive APCs.  Green: other immune cells.",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey25")
    )
  )
```
